title: EG4 · Live Power Flow
description: EG4 12000XP (off-grid) live power flow: solar, battery, loads and generator input, from the EG4 cloud via lux-mon.

links.title: Energy
links.tooltip: EG4 · Energy — daily, monthly and lifetime energy

panels.title: Live power flow
panels.description: Latest reading of each flow in the selected range. Solar = PV1 + PV2 (per-MPPT power). Battery shows magnitude with direction (arrow toward the battery = charging, toward the inverter = discharging) and SOC. Loads = inverter backup (EPS) output, i.e. what the house draws on this off-grid system; L1-N / L2-N are the portal's per-leg readings and need not add up exactly to the total. Inverter mode is the working-mode code (192 = PV + battery off-grid, 64 = battery off-grid). Generator / AC input is drawn dashed in neutral grey (its orange is kept for its own panel); its arrowhead appears only while a source is connected (voltage > 0), and there is no generator power reading, only voltage and frequency. Arrowheads disappear when a flow is 0 W. Source: EG4 cloud (cloud_http): a new point arrives only when EG4 publishes, about every 1-2 min (sometimes up to 5 min); nothing is written in between. Check the 'Freshness' panel before trusting these as live.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "luxmon")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "luxmon_register" and r._field == "value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.name =~ /^(pv1_power|pv2_power|charge_power|discharge_power|soc|eps_power|eps_power_l1|eps_power_l2|gen_voltage|gen_frequency|state)$/)
  |> last()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> keep(columns: ["name", "_value"])
  |> pivot(rowKey: [], columnKey: ["name"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      solar: r.pv1_power + r.pv2_power,
      pv1: r.pv1_power,
      pv2: r.pv2_power,
      battery: r.charge_power - r.discharge_power,
      battery_abs: if r.charge_power >= r.discharge_power then r.charge_power - r.discharge_power else r.discharge_power - r.charge_power,
      soc: r.soc,
      load: r.eps_power,
      load_l1: r.eps_power_l1,
      load_l2: r.eps_power_l2,
      gen_v: r.gen_voltage,
      gen_hz: r.gen_frequency,
      state: r.state,
  }))

panels.title: SOC
panels.description: Battery state of charge (%), latest reading in the selected range; sparkline = the range. Register 'soc'. Source: EG4 cloud (cloud_http). A new point arrives only when EG4 publishes, about every 1-2 min (sometimes up to 5 min); nothing is written in between.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "luxmon")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "luxmon_register" and r._field == "value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.name =~ /^(soc)$/)
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: last, createEmpty: false)
  |> group()
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "name", "_value"])
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["name"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      _time: r._time,
      "State of charge": r.soc,
  }))

panels.title: Freshness
panels.description: Time since the newest point was written (register 'soc', looks back 30 days, always relative to now, not the time picker). Live < 5 min, Delayed 5-15 min, Stale ≥ 15 min. The EG4 cloud normally publishes every 1-2 min, occasionally up to 5 min, so short 'Delayed' blips can be normal; the cloud's own reading is typically another ~1 min older than its write time. Stale means the collector or the cloud has stopped updating and every other number on this dashboard is old.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "luxmon")
  |> range(start: -30d)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "luxmon_register" and r.name == "soc" and r._field == "value")
  |> last()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      "Since last point": float(v: int(v: now()) - int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0,
      "Status": float(v: int(v: now()) - int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0,
  }))

panels.title: Generator
panels.description: Generator (AC input) voltage and frequency, latest reading; sparkline = selected range. 0 V means no generator connected. There is no generator power register, so only voltage and frequency are shown. Kept in its own panel so its colour never shares a chart with Solar / Battery / Load. Source: EG4 cloud (cloud_http). A new point arrives only when EG4 publishes, about every 1-2 min (sometimes up to 5 min); nothing is written in between.

panels.title: Power — last 24 h
panels.description: Solar (PV1 + PV2), battery (signed: above 0 = charging, below 0 = discharging) and load (backup/EPS output = house consumption), in watts. Always the last 24 h, independent of the dashboard time picker. Points are averaged per display interval. Source: EG4 cloud (cloud_http). A new point arrives only when EG4 publishes, about every 1-2 min (sometimes up to 5 min); nothing is written in between. Lines are broken where no point arrived for more than 10 min, so outages show as gaps.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "luxmon")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "luxmon_register" and r._field == "value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.name =~ /^(pv1_power|pv2_power|charge_power|discharge_power|eps_power)$/)
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> group()
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "name", "_value"])
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["name"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      _time: r._time,
      "Solar": r.pv1_power + r.pv2_power,
      "Battery (+ charge / − discharge)": r.charge_power - r.discharge_power,
      "Load": r.eps_power,
  }))
